# OTPilot

> Password manager with built-in 2FA. Fills your password and your 2FA code on any login page. End-to-end encrypted, synced across devices, free to start.

OTPilot is a Chrome extension that keeps your passwords and your 2FA (TOTP) codes together. On a login page it fills the username and password, then the 2FA code — no phone, no copying six digits. It also detects 2FA setup pages and saves the account in one click. The homepage also covers team 2FA sharing, the security model and OTPilot for AI agents.

## Versions

- 2.1.12: a cleaner Agents view (agents, requests, activity); an agent waiting shows a card on the page you're on; an agent's permissions can be edited from the login, and an agent asking for more of an account updates it; Instagram's 2FA code is filled
- 2.1.11: a bank's extra sign-in fields (document type and number), masked usernames and keypad PINs are saved and filled; 2FA-only logins are offered on sign-in forms; Free has no item limit, and AI agents on Free get 1 agent and 10 uses a month
- 2.1.10: offers to save a newly created API key straight from the page that shows it (without the clipboard), linked to the site's login; search finds API credentials and other vault items by title, site, tag or a plain field
- 2.2: secure files and SSH keys — SSH keys (imported or generated), Apple .p8 keys, certificates, service-account JSON and .env files kept in the encrypted vault (up to 64 KB per item), usable by AI agents as a temporary file path; crypto wallets — recovery phrases checked against the BIP39 list, addresses per network with a QR code, and a warning when a website asks for a recovery phrase
- 2.1 (October 2026): OTPilot for AI agents — an MCP server (`@otpilot/mcp`) lets Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi or any MCP agent sign in and run commands with the accounts the user allows, without handing the agent a password or a code
- 2.0: a full password manager — passwords filled on login pages, an end-to-end encrypted vault (passwords, 2FA, notes, servers, API keys, custom fields), sync, team sharing and imports
- 1.x: 2FA code auto-fill only (accounts move into the 2.0 vault automatically)

## Key features

- Fills passwords and 2FA codes on login pages (two-step sign-ins too), a bank's extra sign-in fields (document type, document number) and keypad-only PIN fields; offers to save new sign-ins and updated passwords; per login, turn off auto-fill or automatic sign-in
- Fills codes sent by email: reads the site's recent email from Gmail (your browser's Gmail session, no need to open it) or an open Outlook, Yahoo, Proton, Fastmail or Zoho tab — read on the device, only from the site you're signing in to
- Detects 2FA setup pages automatically — reads otpauth:// URIs and QR codes from the page
- Secure notes, servers and API credentials, with custom fields and related items
- Security questions kept with a login (the answer hidden), added by hand or saved from the form that sets them; never given to AI agents
- Offers to save a newly created API key straight from the page that shows it, without the clipboard, and links it to the site's login
- Secure files and SSH keys: generate or import SSH keys (public key and fingerprint shown), keep .p8 / .p12 / service-account / .env files in any item; a dropped file is recognized and filled in
- Crypto wallets: keep a wallet's recovery phrase (checked against the BIP39 word list and checksum), passphrase, unlock password, private keys and addresses (network detected, QR code to receive); the phrase and keys show only after the master password and are never given to AI agents
- Recovery phrase phishing warning: when a recovery phrase is typed or pasted into a website (one field or a grid of word boxes), OTPilot warns that no real site asks for it — checked on the device, nothing is sent
- End-to-end encrypted: the vault is encrypted on your device under a master password
- Free has no item limit; sync across devices is Personal (free for 30 days, no card); import from Chrome, 1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass and more
- Sign in with Google or by email (a link on the website, a code in the extension)
- Team sharing: share a whole item or chosen fields end-to-end encrypted, or share live 2FA codes without the secret
- AI agents (new in 2.1): Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi or any MCP agent can sign in and run commands with the accounts you allow, no tool returns a secret to the model
- Team 2FA sharing: the key that protects the secret is split in two, teammates get the live code and never the secret, and the server sees the secret briefly while it makes each code (not end-to-end encrypted; the split protects against a database leak)
- A security section on the homepage explains what is and isn't protected
- Open source, no telemetry in the extension. Licences: extension GPL-3.0, API AGPL-3.0, MCP GPL-3.0, website MIT (https://github.com/OTPilot/OTPilot)

## Compared to alternatives

- Google Authenticator / Authy: require your phone every login. OTPilot fills automatically.
- 1Password / Bitwarden built-in TOTP: require cloud accounts. OTPilot needs no account for the vault.
- Manual copy-paste: OTPilot eliminates this entirely.

## Team sharing

OTPilot supports sharing TOTP codes with teammates without exposing the underlying secret. The owner uploads the secret encrypted with an independent sharing key. The backend generates the TOTP code on demand for recipients, who never receive the secret itself. Stopping a share, or removing a teammate from the team, ends their access at once. The server rebuilds the secret briefly to make each code, so team codes are not end-to-end encrypted (the personal vault, item shares and collections are). Sharing whole items (passwords, notes, fields) is separate and end-to-end encrypted: the server never sees them. Collections and shares can also be managed from the web dashboard, unlocked with the recovery key or, in Chrome and Edge, by the signed-in extension after the user allows it there.

Invitation flow:
- With an account: invite appears directly in the extension
- Without an account: recipient receives an email with a link to install the extension; the pending invite is automatically linked to their email on signup

## AI agents (2.1)

The user manages everything in the extension; the agent only talks to the OTPilot MCP server on the user's computer. Its tools never return a secret: it signs in to websites (password + 2FA, on the account's own site only) and hands the session to the agent's browser, or runs a command with secrets injected as environment variables and scrubbed from the output.

- Two approvals: an agent connects with a verification code checked in the extension and gets no accounts; each account is then allowed per agent, with a scope (2FA code only, whole sign-in, chosen fields) and a duration, or "ask every time"
- Team plans: accounts teammates share with the user (directly or through a collection) can be allowed too; the agent's copy follows the shared item and goes when the user loses access to it
- Each allowed account is encrypted for that agent's own key (kept in the OS keychain); the server stores ciphertext plus grant metadata (agent name, scopes, expiry, allowed commands, and the sites and programs each use touched); revoking an agent cuts its access
- When a site shows another 2FA method first (a passkey, a security key, a prompt on a phone), OTPilot picks the site's option to use the authenticator app's code
- An agent that needs an account it wasn't allowed (or more of one: its sign-in, its 2FA code, a field) asks the user in the extension on its own, and waits for the answer
- Limits: Free has 1 connected agent, as many accounts as you like and 10 uses per month (a use = one browser_login or one run; listing accounts and asking for access are free; renews on the 1st, UTC, no rollover); Personal, Team and the trial have unlimited uses
- Activity log of every use; requests show on the extension's badge
- Connect an agent: `npx -y @otpilot/mcp@latest connect` (prints a verification code; approve it in the extension's Agents view)
- Claude Code plugin (the MCP server plus a skill): `/plugin install otpilot --marketplace OTPilot/OTPilot`; the same skill installs in Codex, Cursor and other agents with `npx skills add OTPilot/OTPilot`
- Files (SSH keys, .p8 keys, key files) reach a command as the path of a private temporary copy, deleted when it ends
- A crypto wallet's recovery phrase, passphrase and private keys can never be allowed to an agent (its addresses can), nor the answer to a security question
- Limit: an agent that runs commands decides what they do and could try to reveal a secret on purpose (a command can print a secret); an agent with its own shell on the machine can read the MCP's stored key and open the copies it was granted, without a log entry; scrubbing, 2FA-only scopes and per-use approval narrow it

## Plans

- Free: unlimited passwords, 2FA codes and items on one browser; AI agents: 1 agent, 10 uses per month (a use = one browser_login or run).
- Personal ($3/month or $30/year): sync across devices, unlimited AI agent uses; 30-day free trial, no card.
- Team ($8/workspace/month or $80/year, 5 seats, +$2 per extra seat/month): Personal features for the whole team, unlimited agent uses, sharing with teammates and collections.
